page: Vultr voc-s-8c-64gb-1280s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance built on the x86_64 architecture using AMD EPYC processors. The virtual machine provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at a base clock frequency of 2.0 GHz. System memory is provisioned at 64.0 GB, establishing a generous 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Attached local storage includes a 1280 GB NVMe SSD, while networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The instance does not include GPU acceleration.

Performance profiles place the server in the top quartile for single-core stress testing and PassMark memory operations, supported by 1026.89 GB/sec cached small-block read bandwidth and 127.29 GB/sec uncached large-block throughput. Multi-core compute benchmarks, including Geekbench multi-core (8979.0) and PassMark CPU (18130.87), demonstrate steady middle-tier performance across multi-threaded tasks, bzip3 decompression (44.79 GB/sec), and Clang software compilation. Instruction set support includes AVX, AES, and SHA-NI, though AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent.

Hardware tradeoffs emerge in larger computational tasks; while small 135M language model prompt processing handles 1012.76 tokens/sec, medium 7B model prompt processing drops to lower-tier levels at 23.58 tokens/sec due to the lack of dedicated vector acceleration. However, the balance of substantial RAM capacity and fast NVMe storage delivers high operational efficiency for memory-heavy workloads, in-memory caching layers such as Redis (measured at 15.7 million SET ops/sec), relational database hosting, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: Vultr voc-s-8c-64gb-1280s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute virtual machine powered by AMD EPYC processors on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores clocked at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 64.0 GB of system memory and a bundled 1280 GB NVMe SSD. The 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio supports memory-intensive deployments, reflected in upper-quartile PassMark memory and stress-ng single-core benchmark scores. Although lacking hardware accelerators and AVX-512 extensions—which limits large language model inference speed—the configuration delivers consistent middle-tier multi-core computing and memory bandwidth exceeding 127 GB/sec for uncached reads. Bundled high-capacity NVMe storage and robust memory density make this server well suited for relational databases, Redis caching clusters, Clang build environments, and enterprise web services requiring sustained memory and I/O capacity.
